analysis.title: Philip Morris International Inc.: US EBIT under pressure in FY27
key_insights: Barclays reiterates Overweight and a $225 price target on PM (price $201.87 on 26-Oct-26, +11.5% upside). PM remains its preferred name in tobacco, ahead of BATS and then IMB, on best-in-class ex-FX growth in European staples.

After Q3, PM reiterated its ex-FX FY26 guidance. It now expects the mid-to-top end of 5-7% revenue growth (Barclays forecasts 6%) and the mid-to-low end of 7-9% adj. EBIT growth (Barclays 7.5%). Adj. EPS including FX is guided to the mid-lower half of the $8.29-8.44 range (Barclays $8.38).

ZYN cans move from 15 to 20 pouches in Q4, which cuts revenue per pouch by about 25%. Q4 is hit slightly harder because PM is also giving short-term retail support to clear the remaining 15-pouch cans. Management expects the transition to be largely complete in the quarter.

US segment SG&A rose to about $370mn in Q3. Management guided to a further c10% q/q rise in Q4, which also reflects the ramp-up of the Colorado manufacturing facility. It expects US adj. EBIT of around zero or slightly negative in Q4.

Management said the Q3 spend level is 'a good proxy for the run rate that we're going to have next year'. Barclays therefore sees limited scope for significant US EBIT growth in FY27 and forecasts US adj. EBIT of $619mn against Virtua consensus of about $1bn.
Barclays expects International Combustibles margin expansion and International Smoke-Free growth to offset most of the US pressure, so it cuts FY27 EPS by only c1% (to $9.08 from $9.17).

Barclays forecasts ZYN US volumes (in pouches) up about 10% y/y in Q4 and about 20% in FY27, driven by wider distribution of ZYN Ultra and more strengths and flavours. It forecasts about 14bn pouches in FY27.
Barclays estimates revenue per can of about $3 in Q3 and about $2.40 in Q4, rising 10-20c a year after that.

Japan IQOS had pantry loading ahead of the October price rise in Q3. Barclays expects a smaller unwind in Q4, similar to Q2. The October increase was ¥20/pack against ¥40/pack in April, and pantry loading added about 2% in Q3 against about 4.5% in Q1.

The April 2027 Japan excise change should be less disruptive than this year's. Cigarettes and heated tobacco units (HTUs) both face an equal increase of about ¥12. This year only heated tobacco was taxed more, which Barclays describes as a '10% price increase over the course of one year with the cigarettes not moving'.

Barclays forecasts IQOS shipment growth of 6.5% in FY26 and 8.5% in FY27, and thinks IQOS can add 14-15bn sticks a year in the medium term. Upcoming flavour bans are in smaller markets such as Austria. The IQOS Iluma US launch is still awaited.

Two geopolitical cost headwinds hit FY26 EBIT. Energy inflation tied to the Middle East conflict takes about 0.5% off FY26 adj. EPS growth, with a bigger effect in Q4 than Q3. Missile strikes on supply-chain facilities in Ukraine take off another c0.5%. Together this c1% headwind is why PM guides to the mid-lower half of its EPS range.
Barclays' US revenue estimates fall 11.9% for 2026 (to $2,932mn) and 32.8% for 2027 (to $2,640mn). US adj. operating income falls 36.1% for 2026 (to $541mn) and 43.7% for 2027 (to $619mn).

Valuation: the $225 target applies 23x P/E to average FY27E-28E EPS, a premium to peers. Barclays justifies the premium by PM's lack of US regulatory risk. Upside case is $335 (~35x P/E), downside case is $95 (~10x P/E).

market_movers.rationale: Barclays keeps PM as its preferred tobacco name on best-in-class ex-FX growth. It expects International Combustibles and International Smoke-Free to offset ZYN price-reset and cost pressure in the US.
Imperial Brands (IMB.L) is rated Overweight, ranked behind PM and BATS in Barclays' tobacco preference. It has no US listing.
British American Tobacco (BATS.L) is rated Overweight and ranked second in Barclays' tobacco preference, behind PM.

sector_views.rationale: Barclays' industry view on European Consumer Staples is Neutral, unchanged. Within tobacco, PM is preferred, then BATS, then IMB.

earnings_insights: PM Q3 2026 adj. EPS: actual $2.36 reported (printed), against Barclays' prior estimate of $2.30 and Bloomberg consensus of $2.36 (consensus as of 26-Oct-26). Q3 2025 actual was $2.24.
Barclays FY26 adj. EPS estimate is $8.38E (old $8.41E, consensus $8.37E), up 11% y/y from $7.54A in FY25. FY27 adj. EPS is $9.08E (old $9.17E, consensus $9.10E), up 8% y/y.
Barclays Q4 2026 adj. EPS estimate is $1.86E (old $1.94E, consensus $1.87E). Year-ago Q4 2025 was $1.70A.
Q1 2026 adj. EPS was $1.96A and Q2 2026 was $2.20A, both reported. Prior-year comparisons were $1.69A for Q1 2025 and $1.91A for Q2 2025.

FY26 estimates: revenue $43,504mn (unchanged vs old $43,516mn), adj. EBIT on Barclays' definition $17,838mn, adj. EBIT margin 41.0%. FY27E: revenue $45,982mn (-1.4% vs old), adj. EBIT $19,379mn (-0.4%), margin 42.1%.

Segment changes for FY27E: International Combustibles revenue $26,129mn (+3.3%), International Smoke-Free $17,213mn (-1.1%), US $2,640mn (-32.8%). International adj. operating income is $19,385mn (+1.8%).
Cigarette volume forecast is -1.2% for FY26 (was -2.0%) and -2.0% for FY27 (was -2.5%). IQOS volume forecast is +6.5% for FY26 (was +7.5%) and +8.5% for FY27 (was +8.8%).
Barclays FY26 equity FCF is $12,193mn (+2.6% vs old) and FY27 is $14,134mn (+3.7%). Net debt/EBITDA is 2.1x for FY26 and 1.7x for FY27. DPS forecast is $6.14 for FY26 and $6.51 for FY27.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight PM with a $225 12-month price target, based on 23x P/E applied to average FY27E-28E EPS.
trade_ideas.rationale: PM is seen as best-in-class in European staples, with ZYN and IQOS expected to accelerate EBIT growth and International strength offsetting US pressure.
trade_ideas.risk: JT making Ploom Tech+ a success, disruptive tax hikes, JUUL's success in international markets, and adverse FX.

risk_factors: JT makes Ploom Tech+ a success.
Downside case of $95 assumes emerging-market FX weakness, ZYN and IQOS supply constraints, and an EU heated-tobacco flavour ban driving multiple compression.
US EBIT stays near zero in Q4 and the Q3 cost run rate persists through FY27.
Geopolitical cost headwinds (Middle East energy inflation, Ukraine supply-chain strikes) of about 1% to FY26 adj. EPS growth.
geopolitical: Energy-related inflation linked to the Middle East conflict raises PM's costs, with a bigger effect in Q4 than Q3.
Missile strikes on some facilities in PM's supply chain in Ukraine disrupt operations and costs.

tension_points.bull_case: Better cost absorption as volumes grow, ZYN US volume growth of about 20% in FY27, and expanding International Combustibles margins and International Smoke-Free growth should offset US pressure. Barclays cuts FY27 EPS by only c1%.
tension_points.bear_case: The ZYN 20-pouch price reset cuts revenue per pouch about 25%, and Q3 SG&A of about $370mn is a run rate for next year. Barclays sees limited scope for significant US EBIT growth, with a $619mn forecast against consensus of about $1bn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Q4 US adj. EBIT materially worse than around zero or slightly negative, or Q3 spend levels not holding as the FY27 run rate.
